title: Washboard Road
description: The corrugation instability that ripples dirt and gravel roads. A sprung wheel rolls a looped road at speed, and every time it lands it scrapes grains and throws them a little downstream, so faint bumps grow into a regular washboard that marches along the road. A background process runs many fast passes so the pattern forms in seconds while one wheel rolls and bounces on the current surface for show, kicking up dust on the hard hits. Speed sets the ripple spacing; suspension bounce, scrape strength, downstream drift, grain slump, formation rate, dust and dirt hue are live. The mic feeds the formation rate.
